stem:
The elements phosphorus, sulfur and chlorine are in Period 3 of the Periodic Table.

Table 1.1 shows some properties of the elements P to $\text{Cl}$.

The first ionisation energy of S is **not** shown.

Table 1.1

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Complete Table 1.1 to show the number of electrons in the 3p subshell and the total number of unpaired electrons in an atom of P, S and $\text{Cl}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Construct an equation to represent the first ionisation energy of P.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
Three possible values for the first ionisation energy of S are given.

$1000\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ $1160\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ $1320\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

Circle the correct value.

Explain your choice by comparing your chosen value to those of P and $\text{Cl}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{P}^{3-}$, $\text{S}^{2-}$ and $\text{Cl}^{-}$ have the same number of electrons.
parts.text: Give the full electronic configuration of $\text{P}^{3-}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
State the trend in ionic radius shown by $\text{P}^{3-}$, $\text{S}^{2-}$ and $\text{Cl}^{-}$.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A student does three tests on separate samples of $\text{NaCl}\text{(aq)}$.

Complete Table 1.2 with the observations the student makes in each test.

Table 1.2

| test | test | observations |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | addition of a few drops of $\text{Br}_{2}\text{(aq)}$ |  |
| 2 | addition of a few drops of concentrated $\text{H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ |  |
| 3 | addition of a few drops of dilute $\text{AgNO}_{3}\text{(aq)}$ |  |

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{POCl}_{3}$ shows similar chemical properties to $\text{PCl}_{5}$.

$\text{POCl}_{3}$ has a melting point of $1^{\circ}\text{C}$ and a boiling point of $106^{\circ}\text{C}$.

$\text{POCl}_{3}$ reacts vigorously with water, forming misty fumes and an acidic solution.
parts.text: Explain how the information in **(d)** suggests the structure and bonding of $\text{POCl}_{3}$ is simple covalent.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Construct an equation for the reaction of $\text{POCl}_{3}$ with water.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
$\text{POCl}_{3}$ contains a double covalent bond between P and O.

Complete the dot-and-cross diagram, in Fig. 1.1, to show the bonding in $\text{POCl}_{3}$.

Show outer shell electrons only.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

Fig. 1.1

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{POCl}_{3}\text{(g)}$ forms when $\text{PCl}_{3}\text{(g)}$ reacts with $\text{O}_{2}\text{(g)}$.

$$2\text{PCl}_{3}\text{(g)} + \text{O}_{2}\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{POCl}_{3}\text{(g)}$$

Table 1.3 gives some relevant data.

Table 1.3

| process | value/$\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| enthalpy change of formation of $\text{PCl}_{3}\text{(g)}$ | -289 |
| enthalpy change of formation of $\text{POCl}_{3}\text{(g)}$ | -592 |
| $\text{O}_{2}\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{O(g)}$ | +496 |
parts.text: Define enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_{\text{f}}$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the bond energy of P=O in $\text{POCl}_{3}$ using the data in Table 1.3.

Show your working.
